mainTopic: Pressuring a father over a dowry, and when a wife's sale or forgiveness of her כתובה affects the כתובת בנין דכרין, her מזונות, and the כתובה of an אֲרוּסָה who dies.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story. רב פפא brings יהודה בר מרימר to the house of אבא סוראה. יהודה refuses to go in because his presence would pressure the father into a bigger dowry. When he is made to enter, he sits silently, and the father writes over everything he owns. יהודה says he never wanted this, but he tells the father not to become someone who goes back on his word. Next, רב יימר and רבא discuss whether a wife who sells or forgives her כתובה keeps the כתובת בנין דכרין for her sons. רבא concludes that selling, even to the husband, keeps it, because money pressure is behind it, while freely forgiving loses it. A challenge from the יבמות case is answered: there, the loss is a special קנס. רבי אלעזר then rules that a wife who forgives her כתובה also loses her מזונות, and רב חסדא protests strongly. Finally, the גמרא asks whether an אֲרוּסָה who dies has a כתובה, and אביי begins a response to ריש לקיש's ruling that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא guesses why יהודה does not want to go in
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא sees that יהודה בר מרימר is uncomfortable going into the house. He asks if the reason is שמואל's warning not to take part in moving an inheritance away from its heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא saw that he was not comfortable. He said to him: What is on your mind? Is it because שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Sharp one, do not take part in moving an inheritance, even from a bad son to a good son, because nobody knows what children will come from him, and all the more so from a son to a daughter'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא notices his companion is reluctant. He asks whether the reason is a teaching of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל taught that you should not help redirect an inheritance, because even a bad son may have good children. Moving money from a son to a daughter is even worse, because the daughter is not an heir at all. A large dowry takes money that the sons would otherwise inherit, so רב פפא suspects this is what bothers יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: it is pleasing / acceptable to him
what is on your mind? what is your reasoning?
moving an inheritance away from its natural heir
sharp one (a nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה)

phrases.english: He saw that it was not pleasing to him,
phrases.notes: רב פפא is the one who sees, and it's יהודה בר מרימר who isn't comfortable going into the house.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is on your mind?

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Is it because Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda:
Sharp one, do not be involved in transferring an inheritance
even from a bad son to a good son,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא יְדִיעָא מַאי זַרְעָא נָפֵיק מִינֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: since it is not known what offspring will come from him,
and all the more so from a son to a daughter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this part of the story by naming the possible reason for יהודה's reluctance.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether יהודה's hesitation comes from שמואל's rule against moving an inheritance away from sons.

steps.title: A dowry is itself an enactment of the Sages
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers his own suggested worry: giving a daughter a dowry is a תקנת חכמים, as רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is an enactment of the Sages, as רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא removes the worry from step 1. Giving a dowry is not a wrongful shifting of inheritance, because the חכמים themselves set it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's warning is about moving money away from heirs against the normal order. Here the חכמים themselves made a rule that a father should give his daughter a share. So helping a dowry happen is following a תקנה, not breaking שמואל's advice.

keyTerms.meaning: in the name of (when quoting a teacher)

phrases.english: This too is an enactment of the Sages,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
phrases.notes: He doesn't repeat the quote here. It points back to the teaching earlier on the daf, that a father should give his daughter a dowry like a son's share.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the concern raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case falls under a rabbinic enactment, so the general warning does not apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Helping a daughter get a big dowry looks like moving an inheritance away from the sons.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dowry is a תקנת חכמים, so supporting it is proper.

steps.title: יהודה: the enactment only applies when the father gives willingly
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בר מרימר pushes back: the תקנה is only for a father who gives of his own free will. Should we also pressure him?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies when he gives willingly. Should we also force him?
steps.whatsHappening: יהודה challenges רב פפא's answer. He agrees there is a תקנה but says it does not allow pressuring the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תקנה encourages a father to give, but it does not take away his choice. יהודה's worry is about using pressure, not about the dowry itself.

phrases.english: He said to him: These words apply when it is of his own will.
Should one force him as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 2 by narrowing the תקנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the תקנה makes their visit proper.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תקנה covers only voluntary giving, while their visit would push the father to give more.

steps.title: רב פפא: go in, but do not pressure him
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא clarifies that he never asked יהודה to force anyone. He only asked him to come in without pressuring.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did I tell you to go in and force him? I said go in and do not force him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. He agrees that forcing is wrong, but says simply entering is not forcing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא separates being present from applying pressure. In his view יהודה can come in as a guest and say nothing about money.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say...? (introduces a surprised question)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ מִי קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ
phrases.english: He said to him: Was I saying to you
that you should go in and force him?
I am saying go in and do not force him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the request: entering without pressure.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Going in means pressuring the father.
steps.terutzMaskana: One can enter without forcing anything.

steps.title: יהודה: my very entering is pressure
steps.stepSummary: יהודה rejects the distinction. Because of who he is, his presence alone would push the father to give more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My entering is itself forcing him.
steps.whatsHappening: יהודה pushes back on רב פפא's answer. He says there is no way for him to enter without pressure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an important guest, just showing up creates pressure, because the host will want to honor him. So the line between entering and forcing disappears in his case.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַעֲלַאי דִּידִי הַיְינוּ עִשֻּׂיֵיהּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: My own entering is the same as forcing him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The distinction between entering and forcing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An important person's presence is pressure all by itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how careful a person must be not to pressure others, even without saying a word.

steps.title: יהודה goes in silently and the father gives everything
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא makes יהודה go in. He sits silently, and אבא סוראה, thinking he is angry, writes all his property into the dowry.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forced him and he went in. He was silent and sat. The father thought he was angry, so he wrote over everything he had.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward. What יהודה feared actually happens: his silent presence makes the father give everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה says nothing, but the father reads his silence as anger about a small dowry. This proves יהודה's point from step 5 that his presence alone works as pressure.

phrases.english: He forced him, and he entered.
He was silent and sat.
That man thought: He is angry.
He wrote over to her everything that he had.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows step 5's fear coming true.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The guest's silence alone pushed the father to give his entire estate.

steps.title: The father begs יהודה to speak
steps.stepSummary: Seeing יהודה still silent, אבא סוראה asks if he will still not speak, swearing that he has left nothing for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end he said to him: Even now the master will not speak? By the master's life, I have not left anything for myself.
steps.whatsHappening: The father, still worried, asks יהודה why he is silent even after he has given everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how strong the pressure was. The father gave away his whole estate and still felt he had not done enough.

keyTerms.meaning: by the master's life (a form of oath)

phrases.english: In the end he said to him:
Even now the master will not speak?

phrases.aramaic: חַיֵּי דְּמָר, לָא שְׁבַיקִי מִידֵּי לְנַפְשַׁאי.
phrases.english: By the master's life, I have not left anything for myself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after the father writes his property over.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why יהודה remains silent and what more he could want.

steps.title: יהודה: I did not want this at all
steps.stepSummary: יהודה tells the father that if he gave because of him, then even what he already wrote is not to his liking.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is because of me, even this that you wrote is not acceptable to me.
steps.whatsHappening: יהודה finally speaks and explains that he never wanted the father to give more because of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His silence was not a demand. He objects to a gift made only out of pressure from his presence.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is because of me,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ הַאי נָמֵי דִּכְתַבְתְּ לָא נִיחָא לִי.
phrases.english: even this which you wrote is also not pleasing to me.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the father's question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: יהודה did not want the father to give anything because of pressure from him.

steps.title: Do not become someone who goes back on his word
steps.stepSummary: The father offers to take back his gift. יהודה tells him he never meant for him to become a person who retracts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then now I will take it back. He said to him: I did not say you should make yourself someone who retracts.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The father offers to undo the gift, and יהודה tells him to keep his word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה did not want the pressure, but once the father committed, going back on his word would be a new wrong. So the gift stands, even though יהודה did not like how it came about.

keyTerms.meaning: I will retract, take it back

steps.whatToRemember: יהודה בר מרימר avoided pressuring a father into a bigger dowry, because even his silent presence counted as pressure. Once the gift was given, though, he insisted the father keep his word.
steps.confusionAlert: Here הַדְרָנָא means a person who retracts. It is not the 'הדרן' that closes a chapter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי אֶהְדַּר בִּי.
phrases.english: He said to him: Now too, I will retract.
phrases.notes: This is the father speaking. He offers to cancel what he wrote.

phrases.english: He said to him: To make yourself one who retracts —
I am not saying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after יהודה's objection in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The gift stays in place. One should not pressure a giver, but one also should not go back on a commitment.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches two values together: do not pressure people into giving, and keep your word once you have given it.

steps.title: A wife sold her כתובה to her husband: do her sons lose their right?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר סבא asks רב נחמן whether a wife who sold her כתובה to her husband still has the כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר סבא asked רב נחמן: If a woman sold her כתובה to her husband, does she still have the כתובת בנין דכרין, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רב יימר wants to know if selling the כתובה to the husband also cancels the sons' right to inherit the כתובה money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה has two parts: her own payment and the כתובת בנין דכרין, which promises her sons her כתובה money after she dies. The question is whether selling her own claim to her husband also sells away this second part.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked of him (raised a question before him)
The clause that lets her sons inherit her כתובה money after her death

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יֵימַר סָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar the Elder asked Rav Nachman:
If she sold her כתובה to her husband,
phrases.notes: She sells him the right not to pay her כתובה later, if he divorces her or dies, in exchange for money now.

phrases.english: does she have the כתובת בנין דכרין,
phrases.notes: This is the clause from the משנה promising her sons her כתובה money after she dies.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין לָהּ כְּתוּבַּת בְּנִין דִּכְרִין?
phrases.english: or does she not have the כתובת בנין דכרין?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב יֵימַר סָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the story of יהודה and אבא סוראה ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether selling the כתובה to the husband also gives up the כתובת בנין דכרין.

steps.title: Why not also ask about a wife who forgives her כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב יימר that he could ask the same question about a wife who forgives her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You should ask the same question about a woman who forgives her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on how the question was framed. He suggests that a wife who simply forgives her כתובה should also be part of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's point seems to be that selling and forgiving look alike: in both, the husband no longer owes her. So why limit the question to selling? This sets up רב יימר's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And you should ask (the same question)
A woman who forgives (waives) her claim

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Then ask the same question about one who forgives her כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the scope of רב יימר's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יימר's choice to ask only about a wife who sold.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forgiving seems close to selling, so the question should cover both cases.

steps.title: Selling is the real doubt; forgiving is obviously worse
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר explains that he only had a doubt about selling, since money pressure might excuse her. With forgiving there is no such excuse, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I only have a doubt about a woman who sells. Even though one could say the money forced her, as if she were being hit with a hundred hammer blows, I still have a doubt. So about a woman who forgives, is there any question at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר defends his question. He explains why selling is the only case worth asking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling has a reason to keep her sons' right: she was under money pressure and did not really mean to give everything up. Even so, he is unsure. Forgiving has no such pressure, so it is clearly a full giving-up, and asking about it would be pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (if even this case is a doubt)
The money forced her (she sold because she needed cash)
Is there a question? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: He said to him: Now,
I have a doubt about a woman who sells,
since even though one can say
the money forced her,
so that I would say it is as if they were striking her
with a hundred blows of a hammer,
phrases.notes: A picture of how badly she needed the cash. She did not sell happily. Even so, he is still unsure.

phrases.english: is there any question about one who forgives?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's suggestion by explaining why forgiving is not a real question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forgiving clearly loses the right. Only selling, which might be excused by money pressure, is in doubt.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the question was limited: forgiving is obviously a full release, so only selling is a real doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forgiving is just as doubtful as selling, so the question should cover both.
steps.terutzMaskana: Selling might be excused by money pressure, so it is a real doubt. Forgiving has no such excuse and clearly loses the כתובת בנין דכרין.

steps.title: רבא's two clear cases: selling to others versus forgiving to the husband
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that a wife who sells her כתובה to others keeps the כתובת בנין דכרין, but a wife who forgives it to her husband loses it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is obvious to me. A woman who sells her כתובה to others still has the כתובת בנין דכרין. Why? The money forced her. A woman who forgives her כתובה to her husband does not have the כתובת בנין דכרין. Why? She forgave it completely.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא sets out two cases he considers obvious, one at each end. This prepares the ground for his own question about the case in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding factor is her intention. A sale to others comes from money pressure, so she did not mean to give up everything. Forgiving is a free and full release, so nothing is left for her sons.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is obvious to me:
One who sells her כתובה to others
phrases.notes: An outsider pays her now in exchange for the chance to collect her כתובה if she is later divorced or widowed.

phrases.english: has the כתובת בנין דכרין.
What is the reason? The money forced her.
One who forgives her כתובה to her husband
does not have the כתובת בנין דכרין.
What is the reason? She completely forgave it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא lays down the two clear cases, matching the logic רב יימר just used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling to others keeps the כתובת בנין דכרין because she was forced by need. Forgiving to the husband loses it because she let go completely.

steps.title: Selling to the husband: which case is it like?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether selling the כתובה to the husband is like selling to others or like forgiving to the husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: A woman who sells her כתובה to her husband, is she like one who sells to others, or like one who forgives to her husband?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now asks about the case in the middle. It mixes features of both clear cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling to the husband involves money, like a sale to others, so maybe she was forced by need. But the husband ends up free of his debt, like when she forgives. So it is unclear which side it belongs to.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
One who sells her כתובה to her husband,
is she like one who sells to others,
or is she like one who forgives to her husband?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two clear cases from step 13 to frame the doubtful middle case, which is the same case רב יימר raised in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a sale to the husband counts as a forced sale or as a full release.

steps.title: רבא decides: selling to the husband is like selling to others
steps.stepSummary: After asking, רבא answers his own question. Selling to the husband is like selling to others, so she keeps the כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked it, he went back and answered it: A woman who sells her כתובה to her husband is like one who sells to others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. He puts selling to the husband in the same group as selling to others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What decides it is the sale itself. Because she took money, we assume she needed the cash and did not mean to give everything up, no matter who bought it. So her sons keep their right to the כתובה money.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back and resolved it

steps.whatToRemember: Selling the כתובה, whether to others or to the husband, keeps the sons' כתובת בנין דכרין, because money pressure is behind it. Only freely forgiving it to the husband loses it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This also settles רב יימר's original question from step 10. The law follows her reason for letting go, not just who ends up free of the debt.

phrases.english: After he asked it, he went back and resolved it:
One who sells her כתובה to her husband
is like one who sells to others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא answers his own question from step 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A wife who sells her כתובה to her husband keeps the כתובת בנין דכרין, just like one who sells to others.

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין brings a source about a woman who lost her rights
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין quotes a משנה and רב פפא's explanation of it. Together they show a woman who loses her כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אידי בר אבין raised an objection. A משנה says: if she died, neither the heirs of this husband nor the heirs of that husband inherit her כתובה. We asked: what does 'her כתובה' mean here, since she gets no כתובה? רב פפא answered: it means the כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. רב אידי בר אבין first lays out a source, and his actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (יבמות 87b) is about a woman who remarried based on one witness, and then her first husband came back. That משנה already said she gets no כתובה, so 'her כתובה' must mean something else. רב פפא says it is the כתובת בנין דכרין, which means her sons lose that right too.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (we asked a question about it)
What is it doing here? What is its purpose?

phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin raised an objection:
If she died, the heirs of this one do not
and the heirs of that one do not
inherit her כתובה.
phrases.notes: This comes from the משנה in יבמות about a woman who remarried on one witness's word, and then her first husband came back.

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Her כתובה — what is it doing here?!
phrases.notes: That same משנה already said she gets no כתובה at all, so how could anyone inherit it?

phrases.english: And Rav Pappa said:
It means the כתובה of male children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a challenge to רבא's ruling that a wife who sells her כתובה keeps her כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that losing the כתובה by selling does not cost the כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it shows a case where a woman who lost her כתובה also lost her כתובת בנין דכרין.

steps.title: Why not excuse her because desire forced her
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין asks: if a woman pushed by money pressure keeps her rights, why not excuse the יבמות woman because her desire pushed her?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why should she lose it? Here too, let us say her desire forced her!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual punch of the challenge. רב אידי asks why the woman in the יבמות case is not excused the same way the selling wife is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, a wife who sold her כתובה was excused because money pressure pushed her. The woman who remarried could also be excused, since her desire to marry pushed her. So why does she lose the כתובת בנין דכרין?

phrases.english: But why?
Here too let us say her desire forced her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection that began in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the selling wife keeps her כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If outside pressure excuses the selling wife, the same kind of pressure (desire) should excuse the remarried woman. Yet she loses the right, which suggests that losing the כתובה means losing the כתובת בנין דכרין too.

steps.title: That case is a special penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the woman in יבמות loses her rights because the רבנן penalized her. It is not an automatic result of losing the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a penalty that the רבנן placed on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אידי's challenge. The יבמות case is different because it is a punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman who remarried on one witness's word acted carelessly, so the רבנן fined her. Her loss of the כתובת בנין דכרין comes from that fine, not from a general rule. So the case does not contradict רבא.
steps.whatToRemember: A wife who sells her כתובה keeps her כתובת בנין דכרין. The יבמות case is no proof against this, because that loss is a special penalty (קנס).

phrases.english: There, it is a penalty
that the Rabbis imposed on her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of steps 16–17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a penalty versus a natural legal result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing the כתובה in any way also loses the כתובת בנין דכרין, as the יבמות case seems to show.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יבמות loss is a special קנס, so רבא's ruling about selling still stands.

steps.title: A wife who forgives her כתובה loses her support
steps.stepSummary: רבין בר חנינא, sitting before רב חסדא, quotes רבי אלעזר: a wife who forgives her כתובה to her husband no longer gets מזונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין בר חנינא sat before רב חסדא, and he sat and said in the name of רבי אלעזר: a woman who forgives her כתובה to her husband gets no support.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about forgiving the כתובה. Now the question is about losing מזונות, not כתובת בנין דכרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא ruled that forgiving the כתובה costs the כתובת בנין דכרין. Here רבי אלעזר adds that it also costs her daily support from her husband. Forgiving the כתובה is treated as giving up a whole package of rights.

phrases.english: Ravin bar Ḥanina sat
before Rav Ḥisda,
and he sat and said
in the name of Rabbi Elazar:
A woman who forgives her כתובה to her husband —
she has no support.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רָבִין בַּר חֲנִינָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from כתובת בנין דכרין to another right that may be lost by forgiving the כתובה: מזונות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wife who forgives her כתובה to her husband loses her right to support.

steps.title: רב חסדא protests: this repays good with evil
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that if the ruling were not from a great man, he would call it 'repaying evil for good,' quoting a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If you had not told me this in the name of a great man, I would have said to you: 'Whoever repays evil for good, evil will not leave his house!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא strongly objects to רבי אלעזר's ruling. He holds back only out of respect for the great name it was said in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife did her husband a favor by forgiving her כתובה. Taking away her support in return looks like punishing her for being kind. רב חסדא uses the פסוק to show how unfair this seems.

keyTerms.meaning: If not for / had it not been
Repays evil in place of good

phrases.english: He said to him:
If you had not told me this
in the name of a great man,
I would have said to you:
"Whoever repays evil for good,
evil will not leave his house"?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ לִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּגַבְרָא רַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts with a challenge to רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that forgiving the כתובה costs the wife her support.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forgiving the כתובה is a kindness to the husband. Taking away her support in return would be repaying good with evil, which the פסוק condemns.

steps.title: A man whose betrothed wife died is told to bury her or pay her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, עולא, and אבימי בר רב פפי, together with רב חייא בר אמי, are approached by a man whose אֲרוּסָה died. They tell him: bury her, or pay her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן, עולא, and אבימי בר רב פפי were sitting, and רב חייא בר אמי was sitting with them. A man came whose betrothed wife had died. They told him: Go bury her, or give her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a real case. The חכמים rule that a man whose אֲרוּסָה died must either bury her or pay her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אֲרוּסָה is a woman who has had קידושין but not yet נישואין, so she is not yet living with her husband. The ruling assumes she has a working כתובה even at this stage. The man may choose: pay for her burial, or pay her כתובה money to her heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman: after קידושין but before נישואין
The marriage contract promising the wife money

phrases.english: Rav Nachman and Ulla were sitting
and Avimei bar Rav Pappi,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָתֵיב רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי גַּבַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: and Rav Chiya bar Ami was sitting with them.
A certain man came
whose betrothed wife had died.
They said to him: Go bury her,
or give her her kesubah.
phrases.notes: She has died, so the money would go to her heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן וְעוּלָּא וַאֲבִימִי בַּר רַב פַּפֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the כתובה of an אֲרוּסָה who dies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man whose אֲרוּסָה died must either bury her or pay her כתובה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a betrothed woman who dies has no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר אמי quotes a ברייתא about an אֲרוּסָה. It says that if the husband dies she collects her כתובה. He reads this to mean that if she dies, there is no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא said to them: We learned: with his betrothed wife, he is not an אונן for her and does not become impure for her, and likewise she is not an אוננת for him and does not become impure for him. If she dies, he does not inherit her. If he dies, she collects her כתובה. The ברייתא only says she collects when he dies. That shows that if she dies, she has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא challenges the ruling from Step 21. He quotes a ברייתא that seems to say an אֲרוּסָה who dies has no כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists the ways an אֲרוּסָה is not yet a full wife. It mentions collecting the כתובה only when the husband dies. רב חייא reads this to mean that when she dies, nothing is collected, which goes against telling the man to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: A mourner on the day of a close relative's death, before burial
Becomes ritually impure (a כהן doing so for a dead relative)
But (in the other case): the word that introduces an inference

steps.confusionAlert: The proof does not come from what the ברייתא says outright. It comes from what the ברייתא leaves out: it only says she collects when he dies.

phrases.english: Rav Chiya said to them: We learned:
His betrothed wife:
he is not a mourner for her and does not become impure for her,
phrases.notes: 'Becoming impure' is about a כהן, who may only become impure for close relatives such as his wife.

phrases.english: and likewise she:
is not a mourner for him and does not become impure for him.
If she died, he does not inherit her;
if he died, she collects her kesubah.
The reason is that he died;
but if she died,
she has no kesubah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling given to the man in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the man must pay the כתובה of his dead אֲרוּסָה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says she collects only when he dies, which shows that if she dies, no כתובה is paid.

steps.title: Why does her כתובה end when she dies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why an אֲרוּסָה who dies has no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the reading of the ברייתא and now asks for the reason behind the rule. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule needs a reason, because a wife's כתובה is a promise she normally gets. The question is what makes the case where she dies different from the case where he dies.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule drawn out in Step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason an אֲרוּסָה who dies does not have a כתובה.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: the wording of the כתובה cannot apply to her
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא explains that the כתובה promises: 'when you marry another, you will take what is written for you.' A woman who has died will never marry another, so that promise never applies to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: Because I cannot apply to her the words 'when you marry another, you will take what is written for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the question from Step 23. He points to the wording of the כתובה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כתובה is written as money the woman takes when the marriage ends and she can remarry. That only makes sense if she is still alive. When she dies, the condition can never happen, so there is nothing to collect.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason is built on the כתובה's own words: it is money given to a living woman for her next stage of life.

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:
Because I cannot apply to her
'When you marry another,
phrases.notes: He is quoting the wording written in the כתובה.

phrases.english: you will take what is written for you.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא: שֶׁאֵין אֲנִי קוֹרֵא בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The כתובה promises money for when she remarries. A dead woman can never remarry, so the promise never comes into effect.

steps.title: רבין reports from ריש לקיש: a betrothed woman who dies has no כתובה
steps.stepSummary: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that ריש לקיש ruled that an אֲרוּסָה who died has no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that ריש לקיש said: A betrothed woman who died has no כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report on the same question. This time it comes from ריש לקיש, through רבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same rule that רב חייא drew from the ברייתא, now stated outright by an אמורא of ארץ ישראל. It sets up a response from אביי in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
he said that Reish Lakish said:
A betrothed woman who died
has no kesubah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new report of the same rule drawn out in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אֲרוּסָה who died has no כתובה.

steps.title: אביי begins his response to רבין
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells the listeners to go and say something to רבין. The content of his message comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: Go and say to him:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. אביי is about to send a response to רבין's report, and the actual message continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sending a message back to the reporter usually means a challenge or a question is coming. We do not yet know what אביי will say, so this step only opens his response.

keyTerms.meaning: Go (said to more than one person)

phrases.english: Abaye said to them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the people who brought this ruling in רבין's name.

phrases.english: Go and say to him:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ אַבָּיֵי, זִילוּ אִמְרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens אביי's response to the report in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's report of ריש לקיש's ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. The content of אביי's message continues on the next amud.
